introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn the difference between the formal 'Sie' and the informal 'Du' in German. This distinction is important in social interactions and helps you navigate various situations in German-speaking countries.
introduction.culturalNote: In Germany, addressing someone formally or informally can reflect your relationship with them. It is common to use 'Sie' in professional settings and when meeting someone for the first time.

vocabulary.definition: a person with whom one has a bond of mutual affection
vocabulary.tip: Freund is masculine (der). The plural is 'die Freunde'.

vocabulary.definition: a female person with whom one has a bond of mutual affection
vocabulary.tip: Freundin is feminine (die). The plural is 'die Freundinnen'.

vocabulary.definition: a person with whom one works in a profession
vocabulary.tip: Kollege is masculine (der). The plural is 'die Kollegen'.

vocabulary.definition: a female person with whom one works in a profession
vocabulary.tip: Kollegin is feminine (die). The plural is 'die Kolleginnen'.
Use 'Hallo' in informal situations with friends or family.
Use 'Guten Tag' in formal situations with strangers or in business.

grammar.title: Formal vs Informal Address
grammar.explanation: In German, you can address people formally using 'Sie' or informally using 'Du'. 'Sie' is used with strangers, in business, or when showing respect. 'Du' is used with friends, family, and people of the same age or younger.

examples.breakdown: 'Sprechen' is the verb for 'to speak'. 'Sie' is the formal you.
'Sprichst' is the informal conjugation of 'to speak'. 'Du' is the informal you.

commonMistakes: 'Sie' is often confused with 'sie' (she/they). Remember 'Sie' is formal you only when capitalized.
Using 'Du' too early can be considered rude. Wait for an invitation to use 'Du'.

dialogue.title: Meeting a New Colleague
dialogue.context: At work, Anna meets her new colleague, Lukas.

lines.text: Guten Tag, Anne. Ich bin Lukas.
lines.translation: Good day, Anna. I am Lukas.

lines.text: Freut mich auch. Sprechen Sie Englisch?
lines.translation: Nice to meet you too. Do you speak English?

lines.text: Das ist gut! Arbeiten Sie hier lange?
lines.translation: That's good! Have you been working here long?

lines.text: Ah, ich bin seit zwei Jahren hier.
lines.translation: Ah, I have been here for two years.

culture.title: Understanding Formality in German Culture
culture.text: In German-speaking cultures, the level of formality is important and reflects social norms. It shows respect and professionalism, especially in work environments. Using 'Sie' indicates that you value the relationship with the other person.
culture.funFact: In Austria, it is common to use formal address even among younger people until a closer relationship is established.

keyPoints: Use 'Sie' in formal situations and 'Du' with friends.
Understanding the context is crucial for choosing the right form of address.
Incorrect usage can lead to misunderstandings.
Practice using both forms in different scenarios.
summary.nextSteps: Try to create conversations using both 'Sie' and 'Du' with different scenarios. Join language exchange groups or practice with friends.

exercises.explanation: You use 'Du' when speaking informally to friends or peers.
exercises.hint: Think about who you would use 'Du' with.
